{
  "need": "Competence",
  "secondary": { "name": "Status" },
  "read": "Freezing in a big moment and then spiraling into self-criticism usually means the athlete's brain linked the high-stakes situation to threat rather than challenge. Underneath the self-blame is a fear that the freeze exposed a permanent limit, not a temporary one. The status piece shows up as shame: they think teammates and coaches now see them as someone who can't handle it.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Protector", "instinct": "Rush to reassure them it's fine and doesn't matter, which accidentally signals you also think they couldn't handle it, and drops the standard of competing through hard moments." },
  "mentorMove": "Validate the feeling without validating the story they're telling themselves about it, then tie the freeze back to brain science so it reads as a solvable training problem, not a character flaw. Hold the expectation that they will be in those moments again and you are going to prepare them for it together.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "Competing in high-pressure moments is part of what we're building here, and you're going to be in those moments again.",
    "The standard is the same: we go into the hard moment, we don't retreat from it."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "How we practice pressure can look different: simulated game situations, smaller competitions first, breathing routines, whatever gets your brain used to that fuel.",
    "You choose how much of this conversation stays between us and how much we open up to the group."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 1, "label": "Empathy" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, come here a second. That moment stung, I could see it. You don't have to pretend it didn't." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "Tell me what it felt like right before you froze. Was it the crowd, the clock, your body doing something weird? I want to understand what actually happened in there." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here's what I know from watching a lot of athletes go through exactly this: your body dumped a ton of fuel into you all at once and your brain hadn't been trained yet to use it. That's not a you problem, that's a rep problem. We haven't put you in enough of those situations in practice. That's on me as much as it's on you, and we're going to fix it together." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I'm not pulling you from those moments. I'm putting you back in them because I have high standards for you and I genuinely believe you can perform in them. That's not a pep talk, that's why I'm already thinking about how we build this into next week. You in?" }
  ],
  "longGame": "Systematically create pressure reps in practice, name them out loud as practice for the brain, and debrief briefly after each one so the athlete builds a track record of handling discomfort. Over time the freeze becomes a turning point story they tell about themselves, not a defining label."
}
situation: One of my players froze in the big moment and is now down on themselves.
